who: Manages two engineering teams, nine people in all. Hands the reading before every one-to-one to an agent. Coaches the under-tens at weekends.

moments.plot: One team becomes two next month, and Priya and Jonas both want the new lead role.

tasks.title: Draw who goes to which team
tasks.notes: Keep the pairs that work. Jonas and the new graduate stay together.

tasks.title: Write the role note for the new lead
tasks.notes: What the lead decides, and what stays with me. Priya asked for it in writing.

tasks.title: Pick a stand-up time for both teams
Plan how to tell the teams
Get the second team budget signed
Book a room for the split meeting

capture.title: Ask Jonas which repos he wants

file.title: Check the move with the director
file.notes: She agreed in principle. Get it in a message before the meeting.

dated.title: Announce the new teams
dated.notes: Both teams in one room, then a note to the rest. Priya and Jonas hear it from me first.

repeating.title: One-to-one with Jonas
repeating.notes: His list first. Ask about the on-call week.

attachments.notes: Two time zones. The people in Lagos start an hour later.

tasks.title: Collect the cones from the shed

agent.title: Summarise what each team owns
agent.notes: Read the service list and the last two months of incidents. Where do the edges blur?
agent.question: How should I split the shared services?
bodies: Eleven services go to the team that already fixes them. Two have no clear owner: the billing jobs and the search index.
Nine services follow their heaviest users. The billing jobs move to the new team, which means a handover for Jonas.
agent.otherBody: Every service has an owner in this draft. Split your way: {answer}
agent.otherAnswer: Keep anything risky with the older team
agent.acceptance: Every service has one owning team.

discuss.title: Answer Priya about the lead role
discuss.notes: She asked if the role is hers. It is open to both of them, and she knows Jonas applied.
discuss.question: What should the reply do?
bodies: Thank you for asking me straight. Both of you can apply, and the director and I decide by the end of the month, from the same three questions.
Thank you for asking me straight. I would rather answer this face to face. Can we take thirty minutes before the end of the week?
discuss.otherBody: Thank you for asking me straight. Here is where things are: {answer}
discuss.otherAnswer: Tell her what the role needs first
discuss.handoff: Your next step: send it before her stand-up
discuss.acceptance: Priya knows how the lead is chosen.

review.title: Summarise what each team owns
review.note: Thirteen services, the owner of each, and two that nobody owns.

review.title: Collect the panel’s interview notes
review.note: Four interviewers, one page each, scores at the top.

faded: Learn to say no in fewer words
